metadata.title: Whole-Cell Patch-Clamp Electrophysiology (gigaseal -> break-in -> voltage-clamp & current-clamp recording) [v0.3 instrument-physics demo]
metadata.purpose: Establish the whole-cell patch-clamp configuration on a single neuron and record membrane currents (voltage clamp) and membrane potential / evoked action potentials (current clamp) using a defined instrument stimulus program.
metadata.scope: Manual whole-cell recording from cultured / iPSC-derived neurons using a K-gluconate internal solution. Covers pipette preparation, gigaseal formation, break-in, a representative voltage-step (IV) family, and current-clamp recording. Demonstrates v0.3 instrument-physics constructs (resistance/capacitance/conductance parameter kinds, step.repeat for the sweep family, acceptanceCriteria for the seal gate). Out of scope: cell-attached / perforated / outside-out patch modes, dynamic clamp, and automated (planar) patch-clamp.
beforeYouBegin: Freshly prepare and filter internal and external solutions; verify pH and osmolarity before use.
Pull patch pipettes to a resistance of 3-7 MOhm and, if needed, fire-polish; keep dust-free.

This JSON encodes an instrument STIMULUS PROGRAM (holding potential, voltage-step family, sampling/filter): acquisition parameters must be entered into the amplifier/acquisition software. The voltage-step family is expressed natively via step.repeat (s6) plus the program table (t3).
Liquid junction potential (LJP) for K-gluconate internal vs aCSF is not corrected here and must be measured/applied per your rig (see s8).

controls.name: Gigaseal quality control
controls.description: Accept a cell only if seal resistance is >= 1 GOhm before break-in (enforced by the acceptanceCriteria on s3).

controls.name: Series-resistance monitoring
controls.description: Track series (access) resistance throughout (acceptanceCriteria on s4); discard the recording if it drifts substantially.

controls.name: Pharmacological isolation control
controls.description: Optionally apply 20 uM TTX and/or 2 mM CoCl2 to confirm the identity of recorded currents (Na+ / Ca2+).

troubleshooting.cause: Dirty pipette tip, unhealthy cell, or too much positive pressure
troubleshooting.solution: Use a fresh pipette, select a healthier cell, and reduce positive pressure before contact
Use gentler, briefer suction pulses or a shorter zap

troubleshooting.cause: Rising series resistance or dialysis of the cell
troubleshooting.solution: Monitor and compensate series resistance; limit recording duration

troubleshooting.cause: Filter cutoff or sampling rate set inappropriately
troubleshooting.solution: Set the low-pass filter below the Nyquist frequency and sample at >= 2x the filter cutoff

safety: TTX is a potent neurotoxin; CoCl2 is toxic - handle and dispose per institutional rules.
Follow institutional biosafety approval for the specific cell source (human iPSC-derived neurons).
limitations: The voltage-step family (range/increment/duration/interval/sweep count) and the current-clamp injection family are representative, combined across sources, and marked needsReview; tailor them to the current/cell under study. Filter cutoff, series-resistance ceiling, membrane capacitance, temperature, and the liquid junction potential are not fixed by the primary sources and are flagged needsReview. Manual whole-cell recording only.
